label: Indicted US-academic "decoloniality" discourse for co-opting Andean struggle
description: In Ch'ixinakax utxiwa (2010), Silvia Rivera Cusicanqui sharply critiqued Northern academic circles surrounding Quijano and Mignolo for turning lived Aymara anticolonial struggles into a depoliticized academic canon.
dialecticalTension: Pits embodied Aymara sociopolitical struggle against institutional Northern academic theory.

citations.author: Silvia Rivera Cusicanqui
citations.work: Ch'ixinakax utxiwa: A Reflection on the Practices and Discourses of Decolonization

label: Reclaimed Guaman Poma's visual chronicle as foundational sociology of the image
description: Rivera Cusicanqui treated Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala's 1615 illustrated manuscript as an ancestor of Andean "sociology of the image," demonstrating how Indigenous visuality theorizes colonial trauma beyond alphabetic writing.
dialecticalTension: Elevates non-alphabetic Andean iconography to critical epistemological theory.
historicalContext: Sociología de la imagen (2015) and Taller de Historia Oral Andina (THOA).

label: Adapted participatory liberation pedagogy to Aymara oral history (THOA)
description: Integrating Freirean popular conscientization with Aymara communal memory, Rivera Cusicanqui co-founded the Andean Oral History Workshop (THOA) to co-produce sociological knowledge outside elite universities.
dialecticalTension: Replaces top-down academic expertise with collective Aymara co-theorizing.
historicalContext: Andean Oral History Workshop (THOA), La Paz, 1983–present.

label: Articulated ch'ixi ontology of unassimilated Andean-modern coexistence
description: Drawing on the Aymara term ch'ixi (a mottled gray formed of black and white dots that never merge), Rivera Cusicanqui theorized decolonial subjectivity as holding conflictual worlds in creative tension.
dialecticalTension: Refuses both nostalgic purity and homogenizing state mestizaje.
